source.title: Emergent One-Third Scaling Law as Attention Tries to Concentrate
source.authors: Yizhou Liu; Sara Kangaslahti; Jeff Gore

record.tranche_reason: The study tests power-law loss behavior using dynamic training time and a proposed softmax mechanism, rather than directly reproducing parameter-, token-, or compute-scaling sweeps.
record.gate_note: The paper measures attention and LM-head entropy, energy-gap densities, and logit coldness as mechanistic diagnostics. These do not directly measure a claim version's named scaling quantity, except where loss scaling is separately reported. The entropy thresholds are analysis criteria, not outcome rows.
record.test_reason: The study fits checkpoint cross-entropy loss against dynamic time (summed learning rate) for Pythia (70M–12B) and OLMo-2 (1B–13B). It finds power-law-plus-constant decay with exponents near 1/3. The paper argues this time scaling equals dataset-size scaling in one-epoch training. This is a different method on V1's token axis, not a reproduction of the original sweeps. It also fits loss of a Pythia-160M student trained with logit MSE, a different training regime (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly correct. The authors conclude that 1/3 training-time (equivalently dataset-size) loss scaling in LLMs likely arises from softmax non-linearity learning peaked distributions, with concentrating attention heads as the late-training bottleneck. In their toy theory this holds for any softmax position and any reasonable loss.
record.recipe_differences: The study analyzes dynamic training time, checkpoint losses, and internal logit dynamics, with toy-model theory; it does not reproduce the original parameter/token/compute sweeps or fixed-compute allocation analyses.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported power-law fits depend on subtracting a fitted irreducible-loss constant and excluding early checkpoints that remain in rapid alignment. The authors also note that the mapping from dynamic time to dataset size may be affected by optimizer and hyperparameter choices.

fits_no_version.finding: In gate-head toy models (softmax, sigmoid/tanh GLU, and attention gates; SGD and Adam), loss scales as τ^−1/3 whenever any softmax must learn a peaked distribution. Theory predicts no power law at small coldness, then a 1/3 regime, then exponential convergence near the target coldness.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Training-time loss exponent of 1/3 arises from a low-temperature softmax bottleneck, independent of its position and of the loss definition.

fits_no_version.finding: Attention-head logit coldness grows about as τ^1/3 at late training while LM-head coldness saturates. This holds in pretrained Pythia, in OLMo-2, and in the logit-MSE student.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Attention heads, not the LM head, are the late-training bottleneck for loss scaling in LLMs.

record.problems: The paper focuses on training-time scaling and states that model-size scaling is unexplored. Its LLM loss results use dynamic time rather than direct token or compute fits, and require subtracting a fitted irreducible-loss floor. The authors also note that gradient noise, optimizer-specific effects, and hyperparameter scaling may affect the mapping from dynamic time to dataset size.
record.rows_left_out: No separate rows for each Pythia size were extracted because the text does not assign individual fit values to the sizes; the family-level result is recorded in R1. Entropy and energy-gap measurements, and most attention-head coldness plots, were left out because they are mechanistic diagnostics rather than measures named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Parameter and compute axes are not tested; the paper says model-size scaling is unexplored. The token axis is probed only via within-run checkpoints against dynamic time, not separate runs at different token budgets.
Not tested: no small-run fit is used to predict larger runs.
Not tested: no compute-optimal allocation analysis.
Not tested: depth, width and shape are not varied at fixed parameters.
Other modalities, repeated data, fine-tuning and transfer are not tested; only text logit-MSE distillation is.
Not tested empirically: no comparison of fitting methods, parameter counting, schedules or data choices on the fitted exponents.

missing.what: Per-size Pythia fitted exponents (eight values, 0.31–0.38, with standard errors).

record.verdict_notes: The only V1 evidence is within-run checkpoints of cosine schedules plotted against summed learning rate. The mapping to dataset size rests on the authors' argument and may be affected by optimizer and hyperparameter scaling, which they acknowledge. The Chinchilla exponent range 0.28–0.37 is cited, not measured. R5's fit-dependence point is an argument without numbers, so no V7 label is given.

versions.untested_parts: The LLM experiments measure loss against dynamic time, which the paper relates to dataset size in online one-epoch training; they do not directly fit loss against token count, parameter count, or compute.
No power law fitted on small runs is used to predict the loss of substantially larger runs.
No fixed-compute allocation sweep or compute-optimal parameter/token scaling is tested.
Depth, width, and architecture are not varied at fixed parameter count to measure their effect on loss.
The study tests an MSE teacher-student training regime on text, but not other modalities, repeated-data pretraining, fine-tuning, or transfer.
No downstream task performance is measured.

The study does not test compute-optimal split dependence, or whether fitted exponents vary with parameter counting, data choice, or alternative fitting methods; it does not compare the original compute-optimal laws.

rows.subject: Pythia family (eight model sizes, 70M to 12B)
rows.operation_detail: Fit cross-entropy loss against dynamic training time, subtracting a fitted irreducible-loss constant

conditions.value: L(τ) = cτ τ^−ατ + L\τ; early alignment checkpoints typically excluded

rows.measure: Training-dependent cross-entropy loss and fitted power-law exponent
rows.baseline: Fitted irreducible loss L\τ is subtracted; its numerical values are not stated
rows.value: Fits are described as good, with exponents close to 1/3; curves from all eight sizes collapse against dynamic time
rows.uncertainty: Standard errors are reported for fitted ατ; individual values are not assigned to model sizes in the text
rows.note: This is a dynamic-time result, not a direct fit against token count. The paper relates dynamic time to dataset size for online one-epoch training.
rows.check: Value understates the record. Figure 4c lists eight exponents: 0.34±0.03, 0.38±0.01, 0.37±0.01, 0.34±0.01, 0.34±0.01, 0.34±0.01, 0.31±0.02, 0.31±0.02, so the range is 0.31–0.38. They are likely ordered by size, but the text does not assign them explicitly. Within-run checkpoints of a cosine schedule span about 128 to 143,000 steps.

rows.subject: Pythia family (eight model sizes, 70M to 12B)
rows.operation_detail: Report raw cross-entropy loss with a fitted irreducible-loss floor

conditions.value: checkpoints spanning early training to final checkpoint

rows.measure: Raw cross-entropy loss and its asymptotic floor
rows.value: Raw loss approaches a strictly positive floor L\τ that decreases with model size; fitting without the constant is described as confounding training-dependent decay with model-size offsets
rows.note: The reported 1/3 law applies to the training-dependent component after subtracting the fitted floor, not to raw loss as a zero-offset power law.
rows.check: There is no result here. The paper only argues that a fit without the constant 'would yield unreliable exponents', and never reports a no-constant exponent to compare. A positive floor decreasing with size is consistent with the standard power-law-plus-constant form, not a partial V1. Use this row as an argument, not a measured fit-dependence.

rows.subject: Pythia-160M student
rows.stage_stated: randomly initialized student trained against a frozen pretrained teacher
rows.operation_detail: Train with MSE between mean-centered student and teacher final logits, bypassing the output softmax
rows.measure: Training-dependent MSE loss against dynamic time
rows.baseline: Fitted irreducible-loss constant; value not stated
rows.value: The fitted MSE loss has a 1/3 scaling tail
rows.note: This tests a teacher-student, logit-MSE training regime; it is not held-out pretraining cross-entropy.
rows.check: This is a single run, fitted only after LM-head saturation was chosen by eye. No numeric exponent is reported, only agreement with a −1/3 reference line.

rows.subject: Aligned softmax module with finite teacher coldness
rows.operation_detail: Analyze loss as student coldness approaches the teacher coldness

conditions.value: small coldness, intermediate low-temperature regime, then approach to target coldness

rows.value: The paper states that loss is not power-law at small coldness, follows a 1/3 power-law regime when student coldness is large but still far below the target, and converges exponentially as it approaches the target
rows.note: This theoretical result describes a finite regime of power-law scaling and a later departure from it.
rows.check: This is a theoretical result on an aligned toy softmax module (Gaussian logits), not language-model pretraining loss. It does not measure what V7 names, so move it to fits_no_version.

rows.note: This is a mechanistic logit result rather than a loss-scaling measure named by the claim versions.
